label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/sentry.mdl, models/w_egon.mdl, models/filecabinet.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, D, C, A where the asset was D, B, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline is an upright waist-high cabinet with a flat cap slab, which fits the brief's console. Front, left, right and back views show no part sticking out or missing. The brief gives no slope or other silhouette detail to check against.

M2.reason: Measured 44 x 30 x 42 units. Height is 42 against the asked 40 (5% off), within the 15% band. The 30-unit width is consistent with a console's depth.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for: two screens, dials, a row of switches. Two dark screens are on the front (a third is on the left side, which the brief does not ask for). The row of six black switch blocks is present along the lower front. The dials are four orange squares in the front view, which read as square tiles, not round dials; the brief's dials are round, so this round part has the wrong number of sides and M3 is capped at 1. The front-left view does not settle whether they are raised or painted.

M4.reason: Regions match the brief's palette: green-grey painted metal body, pale grey concrete-like top slab, dark glass-like screens, orange dial faces, black switch recesses, and yellow and black hazard stripes at the base and top edge. Colours agree across all views.

M5.reason: Panel edges are bevelled, the cap has a visible grain, the hazard stripe is on the base and top edge, and the screens and switch row are clearly marked in their places. The brief asks for no glow or lettering.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric. In the four line-up readings the asset (at D, B, B, D) was never picked as the one not made by Valve (picks C, D, C, A), so it passed.

M7.reason: Upright, standing on its base. The control face (screens, dials, switches) is on the front, and the hazard stripe runs along the bottom as a base trim. The front is clear in the front and front-left views.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. 24 triangles is far below twice the median for props of this size. The underside is closed, the sides and top are closed, and nothing is floating or inside out in the 10 views.
